newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 4.

text.p: THE DOMINION
Police officers on drug charges: Four Gisborne police officers and a former detective were charged on Thursday with offences including drug trading, aggravated robbery and procuring crimes. Page 1.

Beehive relocation plan wins support: The government said on Thursday it would promptly consider a select committee's call for the scrapping of a planned new $94 million ministerial building and the completion instead of Parliament House in the original Edwardian style. Page 1.

Peters won't have to repay Winebox fees: The government would not make Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters repay the more than $1.4 million it had paid for his Winebox inquiry legal costs and fees, Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Thursday. Page 2.

Control subsidy 'up to Cabinet': A decision on whether the government would start subsidising rabbit control work while more research was done on calicivirus would be up to the Cabinet, a spokeswoman for Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Thursday. Page 2.
Decision awaited on dole law: The government has not yet decided how to respond to Australia's insistence that New Zealanders wait two years before claiming the unemployment benefits. Page 2.
Super tax credit to benefit thousands: Thousands of taxpayers on law incomes paying into superannuation schemes will benefit from a new tax credit regime announced on Thursday. Page 11.

Brash bid to halt slip in monetary conditions: Reserve Bank governor Don Brash has tried to call a halt to the rapid easing in the mix of the exchange rate and interest rates in the past few days. Page 11.
Float or sell options on GPS for study: A government decision on whether to float or sell in one parcel Government Property Services is a couple of months away, according to Treasury. Page 12.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD
Ansett hit with lawsuit over Dash 8 crash: Ansett is being sued for negligence over the 1995 Dash 8 plane crash which killed four people.
Telecom dominance worth up to $500m: If Telecom was operating in a truly competitive market its profits would be up to $500 million less, according to a Treasury report.

Money market departs from Brash recipe: The money and foreign exchange markets, usually the target of messages from the governor of the Reserve Bank, Dr Don Brash, sent him a messege of their own on Thursday afternoon -- "you can't always get what you want".

BellSouth intends to stay: BellSouth New Zealand's owner, Georgia-based BellSouth Corp, says it has no plans to dispose of its New Zealand operation following the A$1 billion sale of its 25 percent stake in Australian carrier Optus.

Dairy Board reform plan sparks new warning: Corporation of the Dairy Board is needed to remove the instability of dairy companies locked in a potentially destructive power struggle, says Auckland University marketing professor Wayne Cartwright.
Best Buy creditors looking at 40pc payout: Creditors of failed Auckland computer retailer Best Buy could expect to be paid about 40 cents in the dollar according to managing director Mark Mahony.
THE PRESS

Farmers warn of financial ruin, environmental disaster: Financially crippled South Island high-country runholders may be forced to leave their properties unless the government acts quickly to assist with rabbit control, farmers say. Page 3.
LWR attacks tariffs plan: LWR Industries said on Thursday Christchurch would be hardest hit if it shifted more production overseas and imported more. Page 33.
